summary.name: How to Get Into SRE
summary.one_liner: A personal guide by Alice Goldfuss on what Site Reliability Engineering means, realistic expectations for the role, a career-path approach to reaching it, interview tips, and a list of free learning resources.
use_cases: Deciding how to move from a non-engineering job toward an SRE role
Preparing for an SRE job interview
Evaluating a company's on-call and team health before accepting an offer
Finding free resources to learn Linux, networking, git, and security
Understanding what SRE work actually involves day to day
summary.what_it_does: The page is a long-form career guide rather than a software tool. It defines Site Reliability Engineering as the author sees it, contrasts common expectations with realities of the role, and describes a "hops" model for moving from one's current job toward SRE through skills and networking. It lists key SRE skill areas and gives interview advice covering coding, troubleshooting, and reliability, plus questions to ask employers. It ends with a curated list of free learning resources grouped by topic such as git, networking, operating systems, programming, Puppet, and security.
notable: Uses a networking 'hops' analogy to map career steps toward SRE
Contrasts Google's SRE model with broader industry SRE practice
Includes interview questions to ask employers about on-call and team health
Curated free learning resources organized by topic and learning style
caveats: Opinion-based personal guide; the author notes the resource list is not personally vetted or ranked
Describes the author's own path, which the author says is hard to replicate
Focuses on the broader industry view of SRE, explicitly not Google SRE
